events.title: Pilgrims Land at Plymouth
events.description: According to traditional accounts, the Mayflower Pilgrims began landing at Plymouth, Massachusetts, after weeks of exploring Cape Cod Bay for a suitable settlement site. They established the colony of Plymouth, one of the earliest permanent English settlements in New England.
events.significance: The founding of Plymouth Colony became a foundational episode in American history and shaped later narratives of colonial settlement, religious freedom, and self-government.

events.title: First Crossword Puzzle Published
events.description: Arthur Wynne, a journalist from Liverpool, England, published a 'word-cross' puzzle in the New York World newspaper's Fun supplement. It is widely regarded as the first modern crossword puzzle.
events.significance: The crossword grew into a global pastime and a staple of newspapers, influencing popular culture, word games, and language learning.

events.title: Premiere of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
events.description: Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered at the Carthay Circle Theatre in Los Angeles. It was the first full-length cel-animated feature film produced in English and in Technicolor.
events.significance: The film's huge success established feature-length animation as a viable art form and commercial industry and launched Disney as a major film studio.

events.title: Pan Am Flight 103 Bombing over Lockerbie
events.description: A bomb destroyed Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing all 259 people aboard and 11 on the ground. The attack was later attributed to Libyan intelligence agents.
events.significance: It was the deadliest terrorist attack in the UK's history, prompting major reforms in aviation security, international sanctions on Libya, and a landmark international legal process.

events.title: Apollo 8 Launches
events.description: Apollo 8 launched from Kennedy Space Center carrying Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, and William Anders. It became the first crewed spacecraft to leave Earth orbit, reach the Moon, and orbit it.
events.significance: The mission paved the way for the Apollo 11 lunar landing and produced the iconic 'Earthrise' photograph, transforming humanity's view of Earth.
